Q: variables lose their labels after mutate() function is applied in R A:

The Hmisc labels functions annotate the individual vectors in the data.frame, not the data.frame itself. So the problem is that the as.factor() function stips off the label from the column. You could add a version that preserves the labels

as.factor.labelled <- function(x) {
  r <- as.factor(as.character(x))
  label(r)<-label(x)
  r
}

Then the mutate should keep those labels because this new version of as.factor will keep the labels.

Q: Getting error "class file for org.openqa.selenium.remote.RemoteWebDriver not found" A:

I went from Selenium 3.141.59 to 4.33.0. In my case, I had to add these dependencies (4.33.0 as well):

  • selenium-remote-driver

  • selenium-chrome-driver (if you're not using Chrome, presumably you would need to replace this with your browser driver)

  • selenium-support

Q: Difference between .find() and .select() A:

Actually, select_one can be used to find the first of multiple tags.

Example:

soup.select_one("main, article, .main-page-content, #content")

will find 'article' in the following HTML snippet:

<div id="content">Second Item</div>
<article>First Item</article>

Note only the first occurrence of tag will be returned. if there is not a match in the HTML document, None is returned, making this a neat trick.

Q: How to get line number(s) in the StackTrace of an exception thrown in .NET to show up A:

I was able to get line numbers via reflection

var str = ee.GetType().GetProperty(nameof(Exception.StackTrace))?.GetValue(ee);
